title: Portable Executable Format
description: A deep dive into the Windows PE binary format — DOS and COFF headers, optional header, data directories, sections, imports, exports, relocations, resources, and how the Windows loader maps and runs an image.
author: Underlayer

exercise_decls.question: What two bytes open every PE file, and what ASCII letters do they spell?
exercise_decls.explanation: Every PE file starts with the MS-DOS magic 4d 5a ('MZ') at offset 0. 50 45 ('PE') appears later, at the offset stored in e_lfanew. 7f 45 is the ELF magic, not PE.
exercise_decls.hint1: The DOS header comes first; the PE signature is found via a pointer inside it.

exercise_decls.question: Roughly how many layers does a PE file have from byte 0 to section data?
exercise_decls.answer: DOS header, DOS stub, PE signature, COFF header, optional header, section table, sections
exercise_decls.explanation: The layered chain is: DOS header (with e_lfanew) → DOS stub → PE signature → COFF file header → optional header (incl. data directories) → section table → section data.
exercise_decls.hint1: Start at the MZ header and follow the pointer.

exercise_decls.question: At which file offset does the DOS header store the offset of the PE signature?
exercise_decls.explanation: The e_lfanew field sits at offset 0x3C (60) in IMAGE_DOS_HEADER and holds the file offset of the 'PE\0\0' signature.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is near the end of the 64-byte DOS header.

exercise_decls.question: A file's bytes at 0x3C are 00 01 00 00 (little-endian). Where does its PE signature start?
exercise_decls.options: At file offset 0x0001|At file offset 0x100 (256)|At file offset 0x3C
exercise_decls.explanation: Little-endian 00 01 00 00 = 0x00000100 = 256. e_lfanew is an absolute file offset, so 'PE\0\0' sits at byte 256.
exercise_decls.hint1: Decode the four bytes as a little-endian 32-bit integer.

exercise_decls.question: How many bytes is the IMAGE_FILE_HEADER (COFF header), excluding the 4-byte PE signature?
exercise_decls.explanation: IMAGE_FILE_HEADER is 20 bytes: Machine(2) + NumberOfSections(2) + TimeDateStamp(4) + PointerToSymbolTable(4) + NumberOfSymbols(4) + SizeOfOptionalHeader(2) + Characteristics(2).

exercise_decls.question: A COFF header has Machine = 4c 01 (0x014C). What CPU does it target?
exercise_decls.explanation: IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_I386 = 0x14C is Intel 386 and compatible 32-bit x86. x64 is 0x8664, ARM64 is 0xAA64.
exercise_decls.hint1: 0x14C is the classic 32-bit x86 machine value.

exercise_decls.question: What magic value identifies a PE32+ (64-bit) optional header?
exercise_decls.explanation: Optional-header Magic 0x10b = PE32, 0x20b = PE32+, 0x107 = ROM image. 0x8664 is a Machine value in the COFF header, not the optional header.
exercise_decls.hint1: PE32 is 0x10b; adding 0x100 gives the 64-bit variant.

exercise_decls.question: Which optional-header field is present in PE32 but absent in PE32+?
exercise_decls.explanation: BaseOfData (offset 24, 4 bytes) exists only in PE32, right after BaseOfCode. In PE32+ ImageBase follows BaseOfCode directly and is 8 bytes wide.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is the extra standard field the spec lists for PE32 only.

exercise_decls.question: How big is one data-directory entry, and what does it hold?
exercise_decls.answer: 8 bytes: a 4-byte RVA plus a 4-byte size
exercise_decls.options: 4 bytes: just an RVA|8 bytes: a 4-byte RVA plus a 4-byte size|16 bytes: two RVAs
exercise_decls.explanation: IMAGE_DATA_DIRECTORY = { DWORD VirtualAddress; DWORD Size; } = 8 bytes. The VirtualAddress is the table's RVA, Size its length in bytes.

exercise_decls.question: Why does the Certificate Table entry hold a file offset instead of an RVA?
exercise_decls.answer: Certificates are not mapped into memory with the image
exercise_decls.options: It is a bug in the spec|Certificates are not mapped into memory with the image|The loader needs it before mapping sections
exercise_decls.explanation: The spec says attribute certificates are not loaded into memory as part of the image, so this entry is a file pointer, not an RVA. Everything else in the directory array is an RVA.
exercise_decls.hint1: Think about what the loader maps into memory.

exercise_decls.question: A table is at RVA 0x3A04. Its section (.rdata) has VirtualAddress 0x3000 and PointerToRawData 0x1C00. What is the file offset?
exercise_decls.hint1: Subtract the section's virtual address, then add the raw file pointer.

exercise_decls.question: How many bytes is each IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER entry?
exercise_decls.explanation: IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER is 40 bytes: Name(8) + VirtualSize(4) + VirtualAddress(4) + SizeOfRawData(4) + PointerToRawData(4) + 4 more pointer/count fields(10) + Characteristics(4).

exercise_decls.question: A section's VirtualSize is 0x17BC but SizeOfRawData is 0x1800. What fills the gap on disk and in memory?
exercise_decls.options: The next section's data|Zeros|Nothing — the file is truncated
exercise_decls.explanation: SizeOfRawData is rounded up to FileAlignment (0x200 here: 0x17BC -> 0x1800). The spec says if SizeOfRawData exceeds VirtualSize the extra bytes are padding — zeros on disk, zero-fill in memory.
exercise_decls.hint1: SizeOfRawData is aligned up to FileAlignment; VirtualSize is the true length.

exercise_decls.question: What single field in an IMAGE_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR names the imported DLL?
exercise_decls.answer: Name (offset 12) — an RVA of an ASCII string
exercise_decls.options: FirstThunk|Name (offset 12) — an RVA of an ASCII string|TimeDateStamp
exercise_decls.explanation: The Name field at descriptor offset 12 is the RVA of a null-terminated ASCII DLL name (e.g. 'KERNEL32.dll'). FirstThunk points at the import address table, not the name.
exercise_decls.hint1: It is the fourth DWORD of the 20-byte descriptor.

exercise_decls.question: What does the loader write into the Import Address Table during binding?
exercise_decls.answer: The actual memory addresses of the imported functions
exercise_decls.options: The DLL names|The actual memory addresses of the imported functions|The hint values
exercise_decls.explanation: Until binding, IAT entries copy the import lookup table (RVAs of hint/name entries). The loader overwrites each IAT slot with the function's real address — that is what makes calls work.
exercise_decls.hint1: The IAT becomes pointers after the loader resolves each import.

exercise_decls.question: Which export table is sorted so it can be searched with a binary search?
exercise_decls.options: The export address table|The export name pointer table|The ordinal table
exercise_decls.explanation: AddressOfNames entries are ordered lexically to allow binary search. The ordinal table is a parallel array of 16-bit indexes; the address table is indexed directly by ordinal.
exercise_decls.hint1: Lookup by name starts with a search over that table.

exercise_decls.question: In a base-relocation entry, what do the high 4 bits and low 12 bits hold?
exercise_decls.answer: High 4 bits: relocation type; low 12 bits: page offset
exercise_decls.options: High 4 bits: page offset; low 12 bits: type|High 4 bits: relocation type; low 12 bits: page offset|High 8 bits: type; low 8 bits: offset
exercise_decls.explanation: Each 16-bit type/offset word packs a 4-bit type (e.g. DIR64 = 10) and a 12-bit offset within the block's 4K page (Page RVA).
exercise_decls.hint1: 12 bits address up to 4096 bytes — one page.

exercise_decls.question: What does AddressOfEntryPoint contain — an RVA or a VA, and relative to what?
exercise_decls.answer: An RVA — the entry point relative to ImageBase, not an absolute address and not inside main()
exercise_decls.explanation: The spec defines AddressOfEntryPoint as the address relative to the image base. The loader adds ImageBase (plus relocation delta) to get the final VA. It points at process/CRT startup code, not your main() function.
exercise_decls.hint1: 'Relative to the image base' is the spec's wording.
